cards.title: Never share an OTP
facts: An OTP works like a one-time key to an account.
Banks, apps and companies never ask you to share an OTP.
Scammers create urgency, prizes or fear to rush you.
do: Never share an OTP with anyone
Close the message or call
Tell a parent
Report fraud to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
dont: Don't share OTPs, even with 'customer care'
Don't click links in prize messages

myths.statement: It's safe to share an OTP with someone who says they're from your bank.
myths.truth: Banks never ask for OTPs. Anyone asking is a scammer.

quiz.q: Someone calls saying they're from a gaming company and asks for the OTP sent to your parent's phone. You…
options: Hang up and tell your parent
quiz.explanation: OTPs are never shared. Tell a parent right away.

scams.text: 🎁 Congrats! You won 10,000 free coins! Enter your parent's phone number and the OTP you receive to claim now. Offer ends in 5 minutes!
scams.explanation: Scam! Nobody gives free coins for an OTP. Close it and tell an adult.

scams.text: Your OTP for login is 482910. Do NOT share this OTP with anyone. Bank staff will never ask for it.
scams.explanation: This looks like a genuine OTP message: it warns you not to share it and doesn't ask you to do anything. Only use it if you started the login yourself.

situations: {name} is playing an online game {at} when a pop-up offers free coins. It asks for the OTP sent to {name}'s mother's phone. {relation} says 'Quick, everyone's doing it!'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Never share the OTP
rubric.note: An OTP is a key to the account.

rubric.point: Close the pop-up / don't click
Tell a parent or trusted adult
rubric.note: Adults can check and report it.

cards.title: Bill, KYC and prize scams
facts: Scam messages often come from personal mobile numbers and threaten disconnection or account blocking.
Official companies ask you to use their official app or website.
India's cyber fraud helpline is 1930.
do: Check bills only on the official app or website
Ask an adult before acting
Report to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
dont: Don't call numbers from threatening SMS
Don't install apps a caller asks you to install

myths.statement: If a message has your name in it, it must be genuine.
myths.truth: Scammers often have names from leaked data. Check through official apps.

quiz.q: Which is a warning sign of a scam message?
options: Urgent threat with a personal phone number
A bill you already paid in the app
quiz.explanation: Urgency + personal number + threat = classic scam pattern.

scams.text: Dear customer, your electricity will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM as your last bill was not updated. Please call electricity officer immediately on 98•••• 4417.
scams.explanation: Scam. Electricity companies don't send threats from personal mobile numbers. Check the bill in the official app and report to 1930.

scams.text: Your bank KYC expires today! Update now at bit.ly/kyc-upd8 or your account will be BLOCKED within 2 hours.
scams.explanation: Scam. Short links, threats and deadlines are red flags. Banks ask you to visit the branch or the official app.

cards.title: Strong passwords
facts: Long passphrases are harder to guess than short complex passwords.
Reusing one password means one leak opens every account.
Two-step verification blocks most account takeovers.
do: Use a long passphrase
Use different passwords for important accounts
Turn on two-step verification
dont: Don't share passwords, even with best friends
Don't use your name or birthday

myths.statement: It's fine to share your password with your best friend.
myths.truth: Friendships change, and phones get lost. Keep passwords private (parents can help).

quiz.q: Which password is strongest?
quiz.explanation: Long passphrases of random words are strong and easy to remember.

cards.title: Strangers and privacy online
facts: People online may not be who they say they are.
School name, address and uniform photos can reveal where you are.
do: Keep profiles private
Tell a trusted adult if someone makes you uncomfortable
Block and report
dont: Don't share your address, school or live location
Never agree to meet an online friend alone

myths.statement: If someone online knows your favourite game, they must be your age.
myths.truth: Anyone can pretend. Keep personal details private and tell an adult.

quiz.q: A gaming friend asks which school you go to. You…
options: Don't share, and tell an adult if they keep asking
quiz.explanation: Personal details stay private online.

situations: {name} has been chatting with a 'gamer friend' for weeks. Today the friend asks for a photo in school uniform and suggests meeting {at} without telling parents.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Don't send photos or personal details
Never meet; refuse secrecy
rubric.note: 'Don't tell your parents' is a big warning sign.

rubric.point: Tell a parent or trusted adult
Block and report the account

cards.title: UPI collect-request fraud: PIN is ONLY for paying
facts: Entering your UPI MPIN ALWAYS deducts money from your bank account; it NEVER receives money.
Cyber fraudsters send 'Collect Requests' disguised as 'Refunds' or 'Cashback Prize Won'.
do: Remember the golden rule: You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money into your account
Decline and report any suspicious UPI collect requests received on Google Pay, PhonePe, or Paytm
Verify the sender's VPA / UPI ID before sending any genuine payment
dont: Never enter your 4 or 6-digit UPI PIN when someone promises to send you money
Never approve an unexpected notification pop-up asking for your PIN

myths.statement: Entering your UPI PIN is required to verify your identity and receive lottery prize cashback.
myths.truth: You NEVER enter your UPI PIN to receive money. PIN entry authorizes a debit from your balance.

quiz.q: A buyer on OLX says: 'I have sent you ₹1,000; enter your UPI PIN to accept it.' What is the truth?
options: You must enter PIN to accept
It is a scam: entering your UPI PIN will instantly transfer ₹1,000 from YOUR bank account to the scammer
quiz.explanation: UPI PIN is an authorization signature for debiting funds. Receiving money is completely automatic.

situations: Selling an old bicycle on an online marketplace at {at}, the buyer sends a UPI link saying: 'Enter your UPI PIN to receive advance payment.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT enter UPI PIN under any circumstances
rubric.keys: don'?t enter pin|no upi pin|never enter pin

rubric.point: Recognize that receiving UPI payments NEVER requires entering a PIN
Block the scammer on the app and report their UPI ID as fraud

sources.name: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) UPI Safety Guidelines

cards.title: Spotting fake customer care helpline numbers on search engines
facts: Cybercriminals edit Google Maps listings and buy search ads with fake helpline numbers for courier/banks.
When victims call the fake number, fraudsters ask them to install remote screen-sharing apps.
do: Find customer care helplines exclusively inside the official verified mobile app or website
Look for verified domain names ending in official bank URLs, not random blogspot or mobile numbers
Hang up immediately if an 'agent' asks you to download AnyDesk, TeamViewer, or send ₹5
dont: Never google 'courier customer care number' and dial the first random mobile number listed
Never share account numbers or debit card CVVs with phone callers

myths.statement: The top phone number displayed on Google search results is always the official certified customer care.
myths.truth: Fraudsters easily manipulate Google business listings and buy search ads with personal fraud numbers.

quiz.q: Where is the only authentic place to find the customer support number for an app like Swiggy, Amazon, or a bank?
options: Inside the official mobile app under the 'Help & Support' section
quiz.explanation: Official in-app help desks connect directly to verified support without search engine manipulation.

situations: A package is delayed at {at}, and {name}'s family wants to search Google for the courier company's toll-free number.
scenario.question: What cyber precaution must {name} explain?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do not dial random mobile numbers found in Google search snippets
rubric.note: Fraudsters post fake phone numbers to scam callers.
rubric.keys: don'?t call google search numbers|fake numbers|scam

rubric.point: Look for customer support inside the courier's official app or tracked order page
Never install screen-sharing apps if instructed by a phone caller

cards.title: QR code scams: 'Scan QR to receive cash rewards'
facts: Scanning a merchant QR code in a payment app is an action to SEND money from your bank.
Scammers send QR codes claiming: 'Scan this barcode to get ₹2,000 refund/scholarship credit.'
do: Remember: Scanning a QR code is for paying someone, never for receiving money into your wallet
Only scan QR codes at physical merchant checkouts where YOU are the one making a purchase
Reject any message with QR codes promising surprise lottery cashback or prize redemptions
dont: Never scan an unexpected QR code sent on WhatsApp by an unknown buyer or stranger
Never approve transaction amounts after scanning a stranger's QR code

myths.statement: Scanning a QR code sent to your WhatsApp is a safe way to claim a free ₹500 shopping voucher.
myths.truth: Scanning the code loads a payment debit request that drains money from your linked account.

quiz.q: What happens when you scan a QR code in a payment app like PhonePe or Google Pay?
options: It prepares a transaction to SEND money from your bank account to the merchant
quiz.explanation: QR codes encode the receiver's bank coordinates; scanning them always initiates an outgoing debit.

situations: A message on WhatsApp at {at} contains a colorful image with a QR code: 'Scan to receive your ₹1,500 government student reward.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT scan the QR code
rubric.note: Prevents initiating an outgoing payment debit.

rubric.point: Recognize that QR codes are used to PAY money, never to receive rewards
rubric.keys: qr is for paying|cannot receive via qr|fraud

rubric.point: Delete the message and warn family members about QR reward scams

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI Kehta Hai)

cards.title: Work-from-home and 'Like YouTube videos for ₹5,000' task scams
facts: Scammers recruit students on Telegram/WhatsApp with offers of ₹50-₹100 for liking YouTube videos.
After paying small genuine initial sums, they trap victims into investing thousands in 'prepaid crypto tasks.'
do: Recognize that legitimate companies never hire students on Telegram to like random social media posts
Understand the bait-and-switch trap: scammers pay ₹200 initially to build trust before stealing ₹50,000
Block and report unsolicited job recruitment messages on WhatsApp, Instagram, and Telegram
dont: Never pay 'registration fees', 'security deposits', or 'crypto recharge' to unlock earned money
Never share personal bank account details with anonymous Telegram group admins

myths.statement: Earning ₹5,000 a day just by liking 10 YouTube videos from your bed is a legitimate part-time job.
myths.truth: This is an international Ponzi task scam orchestrated by cyber syndicates to lure students.

quiz.q: You are added to a Telegram group promising ₹3,000 daily for reviewing hotels and watching videos. What is this?
options: A well-known cyber task scam designed to steal your savings
quiz.explanation: Task scams trick victims into sending prepaid deposits that can never be withdrawn.

situations: A stranger on WhatsApp at {at} offers {name}: 'Work from home: Like 5 videos, earn ₹200 instantly, join Telegram.'
scenario.question: What is the only smart response for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize it immediately as a fraudulent task scam and do not engage
Block the phone number and report the chat on WhatsApp
Never send any money or bank details to anonymous online employers

sources.name: Ministry of Home Affairs Cyber Crime Advisory

cards.title: Auditing app permissions: Camera, microphone and contact access
facts: Malicious apps request unnecessary permissions (contacts, SMS, location) to harvest and sell personal data.
A simple calculator or flashlight app has zero legitimate reason to access your camera or contact book.
do: Check app permissions during installation: only grant access essential to core app functionality
Set location and microphone permissions to 'Only while using the app', never 'Allow all the time'
Regularly audit installed apps in Phone Settings -> Privacy -> Permission Manager
dont: Never grant SMS reading permission to unverified utility or gaming apps (steals OTPs)
Never download apps from unverified third-party APK websites outside official app stores

myths.statement: Giving all permissions requested by an app is harmless because app stores guarantee 100% safety.
myths.truth: Apps frequently harvest contact books and background location to sell to predatory advertisers and scammers.

quiz.q: Why is it suspicious if a basic Offline Calculator app requests permission to read your Contacts and SMS?
options: It has no functional need for contacts; it is likely spyware harvesting data and reading bank OTPs
quiz.explanation: Permissions must strictly match functionality. SMS permissions allow malware to read two-factor OTPs.

situations: Installing a free puzzle game on a smartphone at {at}, the app requests access to Contacts, SMS, and Microphone.
scenario.question: How should {name} manage these permission requests?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Deny access to SMS, Contacts, and Microphone
Uninstall the app if it refuses to run without invasive unrelated permissions
Review app permissions regularly in system Settings -> Permission Manager

cards.title: Public Wi-Fi risks: Packet sniffing and rogue hotspots
facts: Open public Wi-Fi networks (cafes, railway stations, airports) lack encryption between device and router.
Hackers on the same unencrypted network can intercept unencrypted data packets ('Man-in-the-Middle').
do: Avoid conducting bank transactions, UPI transfers, or entering sensitive passwords on open public Wi-Fi
Turn off 'Auto-connect to open Wi-Fi networks' in your phone's Wi-Fi settings
Use cellular mobile data (4G/5G) or a verified Virtual Private Network (VPN) for sensitive tasks
dont: Never trust unverified pop-ups on public Wi-Fi asking you to install a 'Security Certificate' or profile
Never leave Bluetooth and Wi-Fi toggled on when not actively in use

myths.statement: Free Wi-Fi named 'Railway_Free_Wi-Fi_Official' at a station is guaranteed to be safe and encrypted.
myths.truth: Anyone can set up a rogue hotspot with a legitimate-sounding name to intercept victim passwords.

quiz.q: What should you NEVER do while connected to free public Wi-Fi at a shopping mall?
options: Log into your bank account, enter credit card details, or change master passwords
quiz.explanation: Financial and password logins should strictly be conducted over secure encrypted cellular networks.

situations: Waiting at a railway station at {at}, {name} connects to free open station Wi-Fi and needs to check school fee payment.
scenario.question: What is the cyber-safe protocol for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Disconnect from public Wi-Fi and use personal mobile cellular data for payments
rubric.keys: use mobile data|disconnect public wifi|cellular data

rubric.point: Do not enter banking passwords or debit card credentials over open unencrypted Wi-Fi
rubric.keys: no banking on public wifi|no passwords

rubric.point: Turn off 'Auto-connect to open networks' in device settings

sources.name: CERT-In Guidelines for Safe Public Wi-Fi Usage

cards.title: Spotting deceptive lookalike phishing URLs and websites
facts: Phishing sites use typosquatting: subtle misspellings like 'micros0ft.com' or 'sbi-update-kyc.net'.
The padlock icon (HTTPS) only means the connection is encrypted; it does NOT guarantee the site is honest.
do: Inspect the domain name carefully: the real address is the text immediately before the final slash (domain.com/)
Type official addresses directly into the browser address bar rather than clicking SMS links
Watch out for urgency triggers: 'Account suspended in 2 hours, click to verify now!'
dont: Never click login links sent via SMS, WhatsApp, or unsolicited emails
Never enter passwords on web pages with weird subdomains (like login.google.com.attacker.xyz)

myths.statement: If a website displays a padlock icon in the browser URL bar, it cannot be a scam website.
myths.truth: Scammers get free SSL certificates easily. The padlock means encrypted, not authentic.

quiz.q: Which of the following URLs is a dangerous fake phishing website trying to imitate State Bank of India?
quiz.explanation: The deceptive URL uses long hyphenated keywords on a suspicious free web domain.

situations: An urgent SMS arrives on {name}'s phone at {at}: 'Your account is blocked! Update KYC immediately at http://bank-kyc.net/verify'.
scenario.question: What tells {name} this is a phishing scam?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: The URL is not an official bank domain, and banks never send KYC links via SMS
rubric.note: Identifies fake domain and deceptive protocol.
rubric.keys: fake url|not official domain|phishing|banks don'?t text kyc

rubric.point: The message uses artificial urgency to induce panic and hasty action
Delete the message and report the sending number to cybercrime reporting channels

cards.title: Screen-sharing app fraud: AnyDesk, TeamViewer and RustDesk
facts: Screen-sharing apps allow a remote user across the globe to see your screen and control your device.
Scammers posing as customer care or telecom officers ask victims to read out a 9-digit remote access code.
do: Never download AnyDesk, TeamViewer, QuickSupport, or RustDesk on instructions from a phone caller
Remember: Legitimate banks and customer service agents NEVER ask to view your personal phone screen
If you accidentally installed one, disconnect internet immediately, uninstall the app, and restart device
dont: Never read out your screen-sharing 9-digit access code or grant remote permissions to a stranger
Never log into banking apps while a screen-sharing session is active

myths.statement: Customer support executives from electricity boards need remote screen access to fix your meter bill.
myths.truth: Electricity and telecom boards NEVER use AnyDesk. Remote access is 100% utilized to steal banking OTPs.

quiz.q: A caller claiming to be from your telecom provider says you must install 'AnyDesk' to update your 5G SIM. What is this?
options: A dangerous cyber scam: installing it allows the caller to see your screen and steal your passwords
quiz.explanation: AnyDesk reveals incoming OTPs and bank screens directly to the criminal.

situations: A caller claiming to be from customer care at {at} tells {name}: 'Download TeamViewer QuickSupport and give me the 9-digit code.'
scenario.question: What must {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Refuse immediately and hang up the call
Never install screen-sharing software or share the 9-digit connection code
rubric.note: Prevents full remote control of smartphone.

rubric.point: Warn family members that genuine companies never request remote screen access

cards.title: Handling cyberbullying: Screenshot, block, report and tell
facts: Cyberbullying involves harassment, vicious rumours, abusive DMs, or exclusion in online group chats.
Retaliating with angry insults fuels the bully and can lead to disciplinary action against you.
do: Do not respond or retaliate with angry messages (bullies seek your emotional reaction)
Take clear screenshots showing the abusive messages, account handle, and timestamp as evidence
Block the harasser on the platform, report their account, and tell a trusted adult immediately
dont: Never delete the evidence before capturing screenshots
Never suffer in silence or blame yourself for someone else's abusive behavior

myths.statement: The best way to deal with an online bully is to insult them back twice as hard in the class group chat.
myths.truth: Retaliation escalates the abuse cycle, leaves a toxic digital footprint, and solves nothing.

quiz.q: What is the proven 4-step sequence to handle cyberbullying messages effectively?
options: Do not reply, Screenshot evidence, Block user, Tell a trusted adult
quiz.explanation: Documentation, boundary enforcement, and adult support disempower cyberbullies.

situations: In a school WhatsApp or gaming group at {at}, someone begins posting targeted insults and mocking {name}.
scenario.question: How should {name} respond constructively?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do not reply with anger; capture clear screenshots showing messages and sender numbers
Block the user on the app and report the bullying to platform moderators
Share the screenshots with parents or a trusted teacher for school intervention

sources.name: Cyber Peace Foundation Youth Safety Guide

cards.title: Morphed photos and online extortion: You are not at fault
facts: Scammers use AI deepfake tools to morph public social media photos and threaten extortion.
Paying money to extortionists NEVER stops the harassment; it only invites higher extortion demands.
do: Remember: You are the victim of a crime; this is NEVER your fault and you have nothing to feel ashamed of
Do not pay any money and do not reply to the blackmailer's threats
Confide in a parent, teacher, or trusted adult immediately and call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930
dont: Never pay blackmailers a single rupee (they will demand more immediately)
Never panic or self-harm; law enforcement has specialized units to deal with image blackmail

myths.statement: If an online blackmailer threatens to share a morphed photo, paying them ₹2,000 will make them delete it.
myths.truth: Blackmailers never delete files after payment; paying proves you can be coerced and leads to relentless extortion.

quiz.q: What is the official national helpline number for reporting cyber financial fraud and online harassment in India?
quiz.explanation: Dialing 1930 connects directly to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.

situations: A stranger on Instagram at {at} threatens {name} with an AI-morphed image demanding money.
scenario.question: What is the vital, life-saving course of action for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT pay any money, do not delete the chat, and stop replying
rubric.keys: do not pay|stop replying|don'?t send money

rubric.point: Confide immediately in parents or a trusted school counselor: 'You are the victim, not at fault'
Report immediately on the National Cyber Crime Portal (1930 / cybercrime.gov.in)

cards.title: Gaming scams: Free skins, robux, and account credential phishing
facts: Third-party websites promising 'Free V-Bucks/Free Robux/Free BGMI UC' are 100% credential-harvesting phishing scams.
Downloading cheat engines or game mods often injects hidden keylogger Trojans into your device.
do: Obtain in-game items exclusively through official game stores with parent supervision
Never enter your gaming email and password on external websites promising free rewards
Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) on your Steam, Epic, Discord, and Roblox accounts
dont: Never share your gaming account login password with online 'friends' who promise to rank up your profile
Never download unofficial APK cheats or unauthorized modded game clients

myths.statement: Websites with names like 'free-robux-generator-2026.net' are official partner reward portals.
myths.truth: Game developers never partner with free reward generators. These sites exist exclusively to hijack player accounts.

quiz.q: A stranger on Discord offers to give you a rare gaming skin if you give them your login password for 10 minutes. What should you do?
options: Refuse and never share your password: it is a scam to steal your account permanently
quiz.explanation: Never share passwords. Real game developers will never ask for your account password.

situations: While playing an online multiplayer game at {at}, an opponent posts a link in chat: 'Click here for 5,000 free gems and elite skins!'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT click the external link or enter any login credentials
rubric.note: Protects gaming account from being hijacked.

rubric.point: Recognize that third-party 'free gem generators' are phishing traps
Report the player's account in-game for spamming malicious phishing links

cards.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): The unbreakable digital lock
facts: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) requires two pieces of evidence: something you know (password) + something you have (phone/app).
Even if a hacker discovers or guesses your password, 2FA blocks over 99% of automated account takeovers.
do: Enable 2-Step Verification on your Google, Instagram, WhatsApp, and gaming accounts
Use an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator) instead of SMS OTP where available
Safely write down offline backup recovery codes and store them in a secure home drawer
dont: Never share your 2FA prompt or 6-digit authentication codes with anyone who asks
Never click 'Yes, it's me' on a phone prompt unless you are actively logging in yourself

myths.statement: A strong 12-character password is so secure that you never need to turn on 2FA.
myths.truth: Passwords leak in corporate database breaches. 2FA stops hackers even when your password is leaked.

quiz.q: What does Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) do when someone tries to log into your account from another city?
options: It sends a verification prompt to YOUR phone that the hacker cannot access, blocking them
quiz.explanation: 2FA adds a physical hardware barrier that remote cybercriminals cannot bypass.

situations: Setting up a new email account for school at {at}, {name} sees an option: 'Turn on 2-Step Verification.'
scenario.question: Why should {name} enable this immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Turn on 2-Step Verification right away to secure the account
rubric.note: Adds decisive second layer of defense.

rubric.point: Understand that 2FA stops hackers even if they leak or steal your password
Save backup recovery codes in a safe, offline physical place
rubric.note: Ensures recovery if phone is lost.

dangerous: click yes on random phone prompts

cards.title: Lost or stolen smartphone emergency checklist
facts: Smartphones contain banking access, private family photos, email accounts, and stored passwords.
Swift emergency action within the first hour prevents fraudsters from siphoning linked bank accounts.
do: Use Google 'Find My Device' (Android) or Apple 'Find My' (iOS) to remotely lock and locate the phone
Contact your telecom carrier immediately to block the SIM card (stops scammers from receiving OTPs)
Log into your Google/Apple accounts on a computer and choose 'Sign out of all sessions'
dont: Never delay blocking your SIM card after a phone theft
Never keep written passwords or bank PINs saved in your phone's plain text notes app

myths.statement: If your phone is stolen, you only need to look for it next week because screen locks protect everything.
myths.truth: Criminals swap stolen SIM cards into other phones in minutes to drain bank accounts via UPI.

quiz.q: What is the most urgent step to take within 30 minutes of your smartphone being stolen?
options: Call your telecom provider to block the SIM card and track/lock via Find My Device
quiz.explanation: Blocking the SIM stops incoming bank OTPs, preventing unauthorized financial withdrawals.

situations: While traveling back from school at {at}, {name} realizes their smartphone is missing from their bag.
scenario.question: What emergency sequence should {name} execute immediately with parents?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Use Google 'Find My Device' / Apple 'Find My' on a family phone to remotely lock the screen
rubric.note: Secures device access and initiates location tracking.

rubric.point: Call the telecom customer care to block the SIM card immediately
Change primary passwords and inform bank to freeze mobile UPI access

dangerous: wait a week before doing anything
assume phone is gone and do nothing
call own phone repeatedly without locking

cards.title: Your permanent digital footprint: Think before posting
facts: Content shared online can be screenshotted, downloaded, and archived forever in seconds.
College admission officers and future employers routinely audit applicants' public social media history.
do: Apply the 'Billboard Test': Would you be comfortable seeing this post on a giant billboard outside your school?
Keep personal profiles private and only accept follower requests from people you know in real life
Think for 60 seconds before posting in anger, frustration, or seeking temporary viral attention
dont: Never post personal home addresses, school uniforms with logos, or flight boarding passes
Never post cruel memes, harassment, or humiliating photos of classmates

myths.statement: Deleting a photo from Instagram 5 minutes after posting deletes it permanently from the internet.
myths.truth: Automated web scrapers, caches, and viewer screenshots archive content permanently in milliseconds.

quiz.q: What is the 'Billboard Test' for evaluating social media posts before hitting publish?
options: Asking yourself: 'Would I be proud if my parents, teachers, and future employer saw this on a giant billboard?'
quiz.explanation: The billboard test instantly checks whether content aligns with your long-term reputation and values.

situations: At {at}, {name} is tempted to post an angry, embarrassing rant about a strict teacher on social media.
scenario.question: What wise digital citizenship perspective should {name} remember?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Remember that online posts leave a permanent digital footprint that can resurface years later
rubric.keys: permanent digital footprint|cannot be fully deleted|billboard test

rubric.point: Pause and cool down; do not post impulsive rants or confidential personal grievances online
rubric.keys: pause and cool down|don'?t post in anger

rubric.point: Talk through school frustrations privately with parents or trusted friends in person

cards.title: Predatory instant loan apps: Blackmail and privacy extortion
facts: Illegal loan apps attract young users with promises of 'Instant ₹5,000 cash with no credit check'.
Upon installation, they steal the victim's entire contact book and photo gallery to blackmail families.
do: Only borrow through RBI-registered Scheduled Commercial Banks or Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)
Check the RBI 'whitelist' of approved digital lending apps before ever installing a finance app
Report harassing loan recovery blackmail to local police cyber cells and the 1930 national helpline
dont: Never install unverified Chinese instant loan APKs advertised on social media feeds
Never grant photo gallery and contact permissions to instant cash apps

myths.statement: Instant loan apps offering quick ₹2,000 cash without documents are generous charitable services.
myths.truth: Unregulated loan apps are vicious extortion traps that harvest contacts and threaten victims with extortionate rates.

quiz.q: Why do illegal instant loan apps demand full access to your phone's Contacts and Photo Gallery?

situations: A pop-up ad at {at} urges a senior student: 'Get ₹3,000 instant pocket money now, zero documents, instant download.'
scenario.question: What critical safety warning should {name} deliver?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Do NOT download or install unregulated instant loan apps
Understand that these apps harvest contacts and gallery photos to blackmail borrowers
Verify that legitimate lending apps must be registered with the Reserve Bank of India

sources.name: RBI Sachet Portal for Unauthorized Entities

cards.title: Reporting cybercrime: The National Cyber Crime Portal (1930 & cybercrime.gov.in)
facts: Reporting financial cyber fraud within the 'Golden Hour' (first 2 hours) allows banks to freeze stolen funds in transit.
The Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) has saved over ₹1,000 crore.
do: Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline number 1930 immediately if money is stolen through online fraud
File a formal digital complaint on cybercrime.gov.in with transaction IDs, bank statements, and chat logs
Report cyber threats, stalking, and identity theft promptly without shame or fear
dont: Never wait days before reporting online financial theft (stolen funds get laundered quickly)
Never delete chat logs or SMS transaction alerts before saving screenshots for the police

myths.statement: Calling 1930 only works for multinational corporations, not individual school students.
myths.truth: The 1930 helpline serves all Indian citizens, coordinating with local police to freeze fraudulent transactions.

quiz.q: What national government helpline number should you call immediately if victimized by an online financial scam?
quiz.explanation: 1930 is the dedicated Indian National Cyber Crime Helpline for immediate financial fraud intervention.

situations: A family member at {at} realizes they accidentally clicked a phishing link and ₹5,000 was debited from their account.
scenario.question: What immediate steps should {name} guide them through?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Dial 1930 immediately to report the fraud to the National Cyber Crime Helpline
rubric.note: Alerts inter-bank system to freeze funds before withdrawal.

rubric.point: File an online complaint on cybercrime.gov.in with transaction details and screenshots
rubric.note: Generates formal police FIR investigation ticket.

rubric.point: Call the bank's official emergency toll-free number to freeze the compromised account/card
